correctness.rationale: Exact one-feature enumeration gives absence probabilities \(a_j,u_j,v_j\); their products and inclusion–exclusion give all eight labelled configurations. Identities \(u_j^2-a_jv_j=p_j^4(1-p_j)^2>0\) and \(u_j-v_j^2=p_j^3(1-p_j)>0\) prove \(B^2>AC\) and \(B>C^2\), and a direct ratio argument proves the third strict determinant. Conditional normalizations \(C\) and \(1-C\) are nonzero. Harris product association and MTP2 closure under marginals give the corollaries. Standalone exact Fraction enumerator checked 780 heterogeneous sequences and a one-attribute rational certificate; finite checks are corroboration, not universal proof.

value.rationale: Random intersection graphs model affiliation-driven networks; triangle closure is a principal diagnostic. This theorem gives a complete finite-size classification of conditional adjacent-edge covariance signs upon observing an absent versus present closing edge, stable over all attribute probabilities and feature counts, plus an explicit obstruction to MTP2 despite global positive association. It distinguishes conditioning-induced explaining-away from positive clustering, not a mere reparameterization or a small numerical increment; the exact multi-attribute law and invariant sign proof support uses in likelihood diagnostics and model selection. Scope is finite independent Bernoulli memberships, not fixed-size key sets.
